Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

shallows 0.1.0.9003

  • Raster input and output now use gdalraster instead of terra, and plots use ximage. Both are in Suggests; terra is no longer used.
  • Grids follow gdalraster::read_ds(): a row-major vector with a gis attribute (bbox, dim, srs). ximage::ximage() plots one directly. Extents in states are c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax), the ximage convention.
  • Breaking: sw_rast() is replaced by sw_frames() (a list of grids, one per output time) and sw_write() (multi-band GeoTIFF with band descriptions and times).
  • Breaking: sw_generate() returns a grid by default (as = "grid") instead of a SpatRaster, and sw_extract() returns the bed as a grid with a source attribute instead of a two-layer SpatRaster.
  • sw_from_rast() takes a file or GDAL source name, a gdalraster::GDALRaster, or a grid. sw_coriolis() takes a state or grid with a CRS.
  • New sw_matrix() gives a grid as a matrix. sw_state(), sw_fill_lake() and sw_fill_sea() accept grids directly.
  • inst/examples/mcrobies-storm.R uses gdalraster (warp, hillshade, GeoTIFF output) and ximage.

shallows 0.1.0.9002

  • New vignette, “Shallow water on raster grids with shallows”: the model, setting up and reading a run, dam breaks and convergence, lake at rest, wetting and drying in Thacker’s bowl, rain and the water budget, Earth rotation, rasters in and out, and the R reference scheme.
  • pkgdown site at https://hypertidy.github.io/shallows/, built and deployed by GitHub Actions.

shallows 0.1.0.9001

  • The C++ interface now uses cpp11 instead of Rcpp. cpp11 is header only, so the package has no runtime dependency on it; the solver kernel is unchanged and results are identical.
  • sw_run() coerces its inputs to the types the compiled code needs, so integer matrices are accepted as before.
  • NAMESPACE is now generated by roxygen2.
  • README is built from README.Rmd, with live examples (Stoker dam break, lake at rest, breached reservoir).
  • Added a contributor code of conduct.

shallows 0.1.0

  • Two-dimensional shallow water solver on regular grids: HLL fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, first or second order, wetting and drying, Manning friction, rain, Coriolis, wall, open and periodic edges, and a mass budget on every run.
  • Analytic benchmarks (dambreak_ritter(), dambreak_stoker(), thacker_bowl()), the plain R reference scheme sw_run_r(), terrain generation and extraction, and terra raster input and output.
